## This year's rise

```{=html}
<picture>
  <source media="(max-width: 600px)" srcset="charts/yield-rise-by-model/output/yield-rise-by-model-narrow.png">
  <img src="charts/yield-rise-by-model/output/yield-rise-by-model.png" class="chart" alt="Two stacked bar charts of the weekly change in the 10-year Treasury yield since the week of February 23, 2026, split into expected short-term rates and term premium, one for the Fed Board model and one for the New York Fed model. ## Who is supplying long-term debt
```

```{=html}
<picture>
  <source media="(max-width: 600px)" srcset="charts/duration-supply/output/duration-supply-narrow.png">
  <img src="charts/duration-supply/output/duration-supply.png" class="chart" alt="Stacked area chart of the 12-month change in debt held by private investors, in 10-year equivalents, from 2011 to August 2026. Treasury securities added between about 500 and 700 billion dollars a year before 2020, turned negative in 2020 when the Federal Reserve bought heavily, peaked near 1.6 trillion in 2021 and 2022, and have been around 0.8 to 1.2 trillion since 2024.
```
